newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Solana says Russia has "misconceptions" about NATO.
newsitem.headline: Solana says Russia has "misconceptions" about NATO.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Wednesday Russia had "misconceptions and stereotypes" about the alliance as the Kremlin continued a verbal barrage over the bloc's planned expansion eastwards.
At the same time Solana sought to reassure Russia, saying NATO wanted "enhanced cooperation" with Moscow and that it would not be left out of a new European security system.
"So far Russia has shown some interest. But there still remain many misconceptions and stereotypes in Russia's thinking about NATO," Solana told the Georgian parliament.

Solana reiterated the alliance's promise that it would not place nuclear weapons on the territory of any new member states, saying: "NATO today does not pose a threat to anybody. It does not pose a threat to Russia."
Solana is on a tour of the former Soviet republics of Moldova, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan.

Earlier on Wednesday Sergei Yastrzhembsky, President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, told Interfax news agency that Solana's trip had "an undeclared, behind-the-scenes" aim -- to prevent any form of integration between the former Soviet republics.
"Having called such a line an anti-Moscow one, the press secretary noted that it was perceived by Russia 'no doubt without sympathy, but with concern'."

Russia and NATO are locked in an increasingly bitter row over NATO's plans to offer membership to some of the former Warsaw Pact states. Moscow says this would jeopardise its security and weaken Yeltsin's government.
